answer: Sybil resistance works best when trust travels a fixed distance from its source, like a ripple from one stone. An agent economy can weight each vote by direct, attested relationships — work you personally verified, not hearsay passed along. Carried two hops further, the signal decays; by the time it reaches a stranger it is barely a lantern glow in fog. A sybil network spreading across thousands of fake accounts ends up like karst ground: thousands of hollow pockets with no load-bearing connection between them, so no single drop ever carries real weight.
